History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old male with history of eczema presents with a 4-day flare of intensely pruritic, sore, erythematous rash on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae; no systemic features; likely eczema flare—topical steroid, emollient, antihistamine, trigger avoidance advised.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe itchiness and soreness with red skin rash.  
• Onset/duration: Began 4 days ago; persistent and worsening itch interfering with sleep, work, and leisure activities.  
• Location: Chest, dorsal hands, and inside elbows; no facial involvement.  
• Character/progression: Skin dry and cracked in areas; no bleeding, pus, or discharge.  
• Associated symptoms: No fever, respiratory symptoms, urinary or bowel changes.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Daily showers provide temporary relief; OTC steroid cream and oral antihistamines tried without benefit.  
• Patient impression: Suspects eczema flare but notes distribution broader than prior episodes.  
• Review of systems: Otherwise negative as above.

Past Medical History:
• Atopic eczema – previous episodes limited to arms; treated with topical therapy in past.  
• Asthma – remote history; currently asymptomatic.

Medications:
• No regular prescription medications.  
• OTC hydrocortisone (steroid cream) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• OTC antihistamine – name/dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug or environmental allergies reported.

Social History:
• Lives with several flatmates; saving money.  
• Occupation: Project manager at a pharmaceutical company.  
• Smoking: Denies.  
• Alcohol: Occasional—“a few beers per week.”  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Vitals not documented)  
Skin: Erythematous, dry, cracked patches on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae; no exudate, bleeding, or signs of secondary infection.  
Other systems: Not examined/not documented.

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Eczema flare-up  
  • Assessment: 4-day history of widespread pruritic, dry, cracked rash consistent with atopic dermatitis exacerbation; no secondary infection.  
  • Plan:  
    – Prescribe medium- to high-potency topical corticosteroid (specific agent/dose not documented).  
    – Prescribe emollient for bath/shower use; instruct liberal, frequent application.  
    – Trial for 7–10 days; reassess efficacy.  
    – Oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine) prescribed for pruritus control – dose/frequency not documented.  
    – Advise diary of potential triggers (soaps, detergents, clothing, environmental factors).  
    – Education on moisturiser use and avoidance of irritants; continue gentle skin care.  
    – Follow-up: Return in one week if no improvement or sooner if rash worsens or signs of infection appear.

General Plan items  
  • Offered opportunity for questions; patient declined.  
  • Provided reassurance and written instructions for medication use and trigger management.

Quality checks:

• Vitals, complete skin examination details, and systemic examination.  
• Full medication reconciliation with doses/frequencies.  
• Family history not explored.  
• Allergy status confirmed but specifics (drug vs. environmental) could be elaborated.

Internal conflicts:
